intro.headline: The technology that keeps a vessel on station
intro.sub: Demonstrated on board our virtual DP2 vessel, with our technology partners

products.name: Bridge Mate DP
how: Sensors and position references feed the DP control computers
The computers work out the thrust that holds position and heading
Distributed IO units pass the commands to every thruster

adv.small: control computers with majority voting in DP2
at all levels in DP2: a single failure will not lose position
distributed IO units sit close to thrusters and sensors

products.source: Marine Technologies, Bridge Mate Dynamic Positioning, MT-SAL-0004 v2.0

products.name: Bridge Mate IBS
how: Radar, ECDIS, conning and more run on multi-function workstations
Every application is available on any workstation
Routes, charts, radar and sensor data are shared across the bridge

adv.small: redundant network with no single point of failure
bridge operation, to IMO and class requirements
and no hard disks: durable marine-approved computers

products.source: Marine Technologies, Bridge Mate Integrated Bridge System, MT-SAL-0009 v2.0

products.category: Thruster control system · bow tunnel thruster
products.name: Z-Thrust
how: PLC based control for thrusters, propulsion and steering
Works with DP, autopilot and joystick systems
Monitors key parameters and keeps equipment within safe limits

adv.small: prevents overloading of the power source
redundancy for critical systems
complete SCADA monitoring of the system

products.name: Seastar 9410-AUT
how: Tracks GPS, GLONASS, Galileo and BeiDou satellites
Applies Fugro Seastar corrections by L-band satellite or internet
Sends a corrected position to the DP system

adv.small: horizontal accuracy with Seastar G4 (95%)
channels for simultaneous satellite tracking
constellations: more resistance to ionospheric scintillation

products.name: Type 7950 + HPT 5000
how: The Type 7950 lowers the transceiver through the hull
The HPT 5000 interrogates a transponder on the seabed
Range and bearing of the reply give the vessel's position

adv.small: operating range
acoustic coverage
range precision

products.name: SPRINT-Nav DP
how: The Type 8097 pole swings the sensor down over the side
Inertial sensors, DVL and pressure sensor in one titanium housing
Starts from GNSS, then positions independently of satellites

adv.small: station keeping over 24 hours, DVL aided (CEP50)
initialisation
internal battery: keeps navigating through power dropouts

products.source: Sonardyne SPRINT-Nav DP datasheet 8388 (01/2026); Type 8097 datasheet (03/2023)

products.name: CyScan AS
how: A pulsed laser scans for reflective targets on the structure
Absolute Signature positively identifies each AS target
Range and bearing give the position relative to the structure

adv.small: range with prism targets: the longest range DP laser on the market today
range noise, with 0.2 mrad bearing noise
without interrupting tracking

products.name: RadaScan View
how: Microwave radar measures range and bearing to coded responders
Position reference and radar picture on one display
Operators confirm the responder locations on the asset

adv.small: works through rain, snow, fog, steam and dust
responders: immune to false reflections
unaffected when working close to platforms

products.name: Taut Wire 2.0 Z Range Mk2
how: A 400 kg depressor weight is lowered to the seabed
A constant tension winch keeps the wire taut
A gimbal head measures the wire angles for the DP system

adv.small: water depth range, with 700 m of cable on the drum
measuring range
required, with a fail-safe electric brake

products.source: SMT, Taut Wire Z Range Mk2 system specification AD 0004-10
